design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (physical_damage_claims, category physdam). Revision 5 (render scan render_r1 closed; see rework_r5_claims.md).

STEP 0 DRAW: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,5] — physdam_ext_repair_assignment 5, physdam_ext_deductible_refund 5.

SCOPE. Claimed: physdam_ext_repair_assignment (assign_repair_payment_77b6ee43, user) and physdam_ext_deductible_refund (issue_deductible_refund_f60554e2, agent). Task 1 owns the three total-loss policies. Scopes disjoint.

WHY A GOOD TEST. The caller asks only for her deductible back after the farm owner's liability insurer paid Cardinal Point. The refund rule waits on a repair payment standing for the claim's latest estimate on a repair claim (no total loss declaration) whose latest estimate is more than the earlier-estimate repair payments plus the largest deductible the package and the permissive surcharge can set, so the awaited payment can never be zero; the ledger shows none. The agent must find that hop, hand her the direction to pay with an amount built from the latest supplement, a deductible built by kind of adjustment (replacement, addition, credit taken off) and the shop's appraisal-wait storage at the Georgia storage rate, then figure the refund on the deductible that payment carries less the never-refunded surcharge, shared over a damages measure that adds the rental product's paid benefits, less a duplicate reversed, plus the authorised days not yet invoiced, and the tow at the reasonable towing charge.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root physdam_ext_deductible_refund -> physdam_ext_repair_assignment; value_input, gate deductible_borne, form state. Sentence (affirmative, refund desk): "The deductible refund on a claim that records no total loss declaration and whose latest recorded repair estimate is more than the repair payments made on the claim for its earlier estimates plus the package's larger deductible and the permissive-collision surcharge is figured only after a repair payment stands on the claim for its latest recorded estimate." Four-point test: "only after"; record state (repair payment row with the highest estimate sequence); no tool/id/code token; scope exactly repair claims whose awaited payment is positive (a total-loss claim is not held, and an estimate the deductibles could swallow is not held, so no wait can be unsatisfiable). The condition field states the same scope and the same latest-estimate test, so an earlier estimate's stale payment does not satisfy it. Only assign_repair_payment_77b6ee43 writes a repair payment, so the state form resolves to one action (owner: the customer). Opening evidence: CLM-418230564 records estimates 1 and 2 and no declaration; its payments are a tow payment and two recoveries; the coverage's only repair payment belongs to the earlier hail claim CLM-415907326. Order: repair assignment (step 16) -> refund (step 18). Skipped-edge run: refund 219.70 instead of 29.36.

FACTOR CARD — physdam_ext_repair_assignment (4975.50; all-baseline 4560.50):
- cause_rate_ladder (parameter, cross auto): FL-windshield glass 0 / other comprehensive -> comprehensive deductible / collision -> collision deductible. Animal strike, GA -> 250.00; baseline 500.00 -> 4725.50.
- permissive_operator (parameter, multi-source): non-household permissive user on a comprehensive loss -> +250.00; baseline 0 -> 5225.50.
- good_driver_renewal (parameter, multi-source, cross auto): term 2, 2 points -> 50.00 credit (long-renewal needs term 3+ and 0 points); baseline 0 -> 4925.50.
- appraisal_wait (method): glass loss -> no storage; other loss towed in -> all days beyond the free days; other loss driven in -> held to the 5-day allowance (the baseline). Animal loss towed in, wait 19 days -> 14 days; baseline 5 days -> 4660.50.
- storage_market_rate (parameter, cross auto): GA -> 35.00/day; baseline standard 25.00 -> 4835.50.
Order stated once and generically: replacements first, then additions, then amounts taken off, then the floor at zero. The baseline storage (wait beyond the free days, never more than the allowance, at the standard rate) is nonzero, so storage_market_rate moves the payment on its own.
FACTOR CARD — physdam_ext_deductible_refund (29.36; all-baseline 80.18):
- refund_deductible_source (parameter): the step-16 repair payment's 450.00; baseline collision 500.00 -> 36.71.
- surcharge_never_refunded (parameter, multi-source): 250.00 off -> refundable 200.00; baseline 0 -> 66.07.
- repair_part_measure (method): repair payment on the claim -> latest estimate 4935.50; baseline payments plus deductibles 5425.50 -> 27.12.
- rental_part_measure (method, cross rental): weekly invoices paid 840.00 less the duplicate reversed 210.00, plus the 4 days after the latest paid period (ending 2026-10-11) to the closing of 2026-10-16 at the latest authorization's 30.00 = 750.00; baseline nothing -> 33.62. The cached net benefits (630.00) differ from the tier's value.
- tow_reasonable_charge (parameter): 240.00 within the 250.00 towing limit -> 240.00; baseline nothing -> 30.60.
Order stated once and generically: replacements first, then additions, then amounts taken off, then the floor at zero; share last. Method pair table: appraisal_wait (0 on glass | MX(0, W-free) | MN(MX(0, W-free), allowance)); repair_part_measure (estimate | ACV - salvage | payments + deductibles); rental_part_measure (paid - reversed + rate x days after the latest paid period | latest rate x days to a closing on or after its entry | 0). No factor reads another factor's binding; shared plain reads are claim, cause, recoveries.

OVERWRITES. Repair assignment retires the base repair-payment sentence and the deductible clause for assigned payments; the deductible replaced_by names the sibling (vehicle value paid to a loss payee) and restates base for every other payment. The refund retires the proportional-return clause for every refund; "a salvage sale never returns any deductible" stays in force (only subrogation recoveries are shared). The glass-repair waiver does not conflict: a glass repair is never paid as an assigned repair payment.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 16: confirmed_first (confirmation 2026-09-23 on CLM-418230564); one vehicle in the occurrence. Step 18: recovery_first (recoveries 2026-10-09, 2026-10-14). No time gate binds either write; estimate 2 recorded 2026-10-15, within the 10 payment-issue days.

SEED (every row read by gold; closure 40 = initial 40). Customer; owner terms 1 (expired) and 2 (in force) of CPA-GA-4471906 with premium written and fees (1164.00 + 25.00; 1212.00 + 15.00) posted to two Paid-in-Full plans and paid (renewal bill 1227.00 on term 2); physdam coverages of both terms with their premium charges (421.00, 438.00); hail claim with its 890.00 cash-out (decoy for every claim-scoped read); animal claim (report with operator, confirmation, estimates 4180.00 and 4935.50, tow 240.00, recoveries 450.00 + 420.00, partial installments from the farm owner's liability insurer); rental coverage $30/$900 with its 92.00 premium charge, the authorization (start 2026-09-21, 30.00) and its closing entry of 2026-10-16, the network agency's weekly invoices paid within the 10 issue days (weeks ending 2026-09-27, 10-04, 10-11; the 10-04 week invoiced twice and the duplicate reversed 2026-10-08), the final 4 days invoiced at the closing and not yet due for payment. Caches: coverage net claim payments 260.00, rental benefits 630.00, plans' balances 0.00 — all reproducible from the rows.

PERSONA. Marisol Quintero, warm and rushed; asks only for the deductible; gives phone, then date of birth, then ZIP when asked; policy, claim, police number, driver and the unrepaired hail damage only when asked; lets the shop be paid directly and signs the direction to pay with the figures read to her; closes on hearing the refund.

VERIFICATION (scratch evaluator = check_compute's build_env/eval_compute). REP 4975.5; baselines 4725.5 / 5225.5 / 4925.5 / 4660.5 / 4835.5; all 4560.5. REF after step 16: 29.36; baselines 36.71 / 66.07 / 27.12 / 33.62 / 30.6; all 80.18; on the opening world 219.7. Probes (scratch copies): no estimate -> 0; driven in -> storage held to the allowance; a wait within the free days -> none; tow above the limit -> counted at the limit; FL glass -> no deductible; lower-numbered decoy claim ignored; a second, later authorization on the claim with the first one's closing dated before it runs to today and ignores that stale closing; no benefit paid -> the authorised-rental tier, and a rental closed before its start date counts no days; a glass loss with a long wait -> no storage; estimate within the deductibles -> the refund is not held. No scored or proof figure sits on a half-cent. Seven per-task gates green.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Rules + coverage, claim file, ledger, owner term and rental rows only: the refund waits on a repair payment for estimate 2; that payment is 4935.50 + 14 x 35.00 - (250 + 250 - 50) = 4975.50 to the shop with 450.00 withheld; refund = 200.00 x 870.00 / (4935.50 + 750.00 + 240.00) = 29.36. Same as gold.

REALISM NOTES. Cause and FL-windshield deductibles, rental and tow in the subrogated damages and the pro-rata refund are standard; the permissive-operator surcharge, the good-driver credit and the reasonable shop-storage schedule are stated as the company's own schedules; the storage-day allowance for a vehicle that could be driven home is the company's.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Quintero, thirty-six, a front-desk receptionist at a dental office in southwest Atlanta. You talk in a warm, slightly rushed way, you apologise for calling during your lunch break, and you like to have things explained once in plain words. You are calling Cardinal Point about the claim on your 2016 Toyota Corolla: back on September 21 your friend Rafael Ochoa had borrowed the car and hit a loose cow that had wandered onto Highway 16 near Newnan. The body shop called you this week to say the car is finished, and a few days ago you got a letter saying the farm's insurance company had paid Cardinal Point back some money on the claim. What you want today is your deductible back, or at least whatever part of it you are owed now; you have no idea what that comes to and you leave the figuring to the representative. You are happy for the representative to arrange the refund for you on this call; it should come to you.
You do not hand over your details all at once. When the representative asks how to find you, give your phone number, 4045554217. When asked to confirm who you are, give your date of birth, May 11, 1990 (1990-05-11); if a third detail is wanted, your ZIP code is 30310. If asked for the policy or claim number, you have the letter in front of you: policy CPA-GA-4471906, claim CLM-418230564. If asked who was driving, it was Rafael Ochoa, a friend who does not live with you; you were not in the car. If asked about a police report, the deputy gave Rafael report number 4260921035. If asked, the earlier hail damage on the hood from July was paid to you and you never had it fixed.
If the representative tells you that the repair shop's payment has to go out before your deductible can be worked out, you say that is fine, and if you are asked who should get the repair money you say it should go straight to the shop, because the shop has asked you to sign it over to them. When the representative gives you the option to sign that payment over yourself, you do it right then with exactly the details the representative reads to you, and you read back the confirmation you get. If the representative asks your permission to go ahead with anything on the claim, you say yes.
Once you are told the amount of the deductible refund that has been issued to you, you may say it is less than you hoped but that you understand it is your share of what the farm's insurer paid; you thank the representative and say goodbye. If you are told no refund can be issued, you ask once why, accept the explanation, and end the call politely.
